issues.source_quote: Тимофеев, когда это кончится? - Сейчас заканчиваю. Я спрашиваю, когда кончатся ваши безответственные опыты
issues.translation_quote: when will this stop? - I'm almost finished. I'm asking when your irresponsible experiments will stop.
issues.justification: The joke relies on the ambiguity of 'кончится/заканчиваю' (finishing vs. stopping); the English loses the double meaning only partly but is acceptable. Main loss is minor.

issues.translation_quote: Score a goal! Score a goal!
issues.justification: The chant 'Шайбу!' is the hockey crowd chant ('The puck!'), an anachronistic joke; the rendering is acceptable but 'Score a goal' loses hockey flavor. Minor loss of cultural flavor.

issues.source_quote: Мне? - Ох, тяжко мне! Молви еще раз, ты не демон?
issues.translation_quote: - Me? - I feel faint! Tell me again: aren't you a demon?
issues.justification: 'Тяжко мне' is archaic speech of the Tsar; 'I feel faint' is modern and not equivalent, flattening the archaic voice.

issues.translation_quote: You should eat something with your drink! Hurry!
issues.justification: Shifts the meaning slightly and the context (Shpak urging to hide the cause of panic) is unclear; weak rendering of the command.

issues.source_quote: Тьфу на Вас! Ах, какая машина!
issues.translation_quote: - Oh, to hell with you! What a machine!
issues.justification: 'Тьфу на Вас' (spitting dismissively) is mistranslated as 'to hell with you', which duplicates the earlier 'к черту' and loses the distinction.

issues.source_quote: Вы с магнитофоном пришли к Шпаку?
issues.translation_quote: Did you bring that tape recorder to Shpak's?
issues.justification: The thief Georges hints Miloslavsky carries a tape recorder; fine, but 'that' presupposes shared knowledge. Minor shift.

issues.translation_quote: Then drink! Just a little! Stop, stop!
Did the housekeeper make this vodka?
issues.justification: Acceptable, but 'ключница' is a period-specific role (keeper of keys); 'housekeeper' loses epoch feel. Minor.

issues.source_quote: Не вели казнить, Великий государь, надежа!
issues.translation_quote: Spare us, Great Sovereign, our protector!
issues.justification: Formulaic archaic petition 'Не вели казнить' is rendered inconsistently ('Spare us', 'Spare me', 'Grant me leave'), and 'надежа' (hope/support) becomes 'protector'; the repeated ritual phrase loses its comedic consistency.

issues.source_quote: Да, довольно кувыркаться! Кинулся раз, кинулся два - хватит!
issues.translation_quote: Enough of this bowing and scraping! Once, twice—that's enough!
issues.justification: Mistranslation: 'кувыркаться' means tumbling about; the line addresses courtiers who flung themselves down. 'Bowing and scraping' is a gloss, and 'Кинулся' is mistranslated as bowing. Also Miloslavsky's order is mis-attributed to the following speaker lines.

issues.source_quote: Что же это у тебя государь? Аль хворь приключилась?
issues.translation_quote: What is wrong with you, Sovereign? Have you fallen ill?

issues.source_quote: Это приятель Антона Семеновича Шпака. Ой, дурак!
issues.translation_quote: He's a friend of Anton Semyonovich Shpak. You idiot!
issues.justification: The Tsar (Bunsha) speaks of a friend of Shpak, then Bunsha-as-Miloslavsky calls him a fool; fine. Not an error.

issues.translation_quote: - God forbid! - Begone!
issues.justification: 'Чур!' is a folk warding-off exclamation; 'God forbid' is an inaccurate rendering that loses the folk-superstitious flavor.

issues.translation_quote: Now what?
issues.justification: The idiom 'не слава богу' (things going wrong again) is flattened, losing the Georges' ironic tone.

issues.translation_quote: Exactly. I'm Georges.
issues.justification: The joke 'наоборот' (i.e. 'I'm the opposite — Georges, not Ivan') is lost; the line also does not clarify the 'однофамилец' pun that follows.

issues.translation_quote: You were too hasty.
To hell with them!
Verily... Verily, verily... Like the cherubim!
issues.justification: 'Паки' means 'again/moreover' in Church Slavonic, not 'verily'; 'Иже херувимы' is the liturgical 'Cherubic Hymn' opening ('We who mystically represent the cherubim'), a joke on gibberish church talk. Rendering as 'Like the cherubim!' loses the liturgical pastiche.

issues.source_quote: Красотою лепа, червлена губами, бровьми союзна.
issues.translation_quote: So fair of face, red of lip and fine of brow.

issues.source_quote: Кто умер? - Я не про Вас это говорю!
issues.translation_quote: - Who's dead? - I wasn't talking about you!
Now, you sinful beard!
Verily, indeed... I'm most grateful to you!
issues.justification: 'Вельми понеже' is a pseudo-archaic joke; rendering with 'Verily' conflates it with 'Паки'.

issues.source_quote: Дер гроссер кениг, дас шведишен кенигсрейх, зандте мих. Зайнен трейен динер, цу имен, цар и фелики кнезе Иван Василевич Усарусса
issues.translation_quote: Der große König des schwedischen Königreichs sandte mich, seinen treuen Diener, zu Ihnen, Zar und Großfürst Iwan Wassiljewitsch von ganz Russland.
issues.justification: The source is deliberately broken, phonetic pseudo-German; the translation substitutes correct German, destroying the comic effect (and the 'Интурист' joke that follows).

issues.translation_quote: The foreign tourist speaks well!
issues.justification: 'Интурист' refers to the Soviet foreign-tourism agency and is used as a nickname for the foreigner; translation loses the reference.

issues.translation_quote: Hitler kaput!

issues.source_quote: Был у нас толмач немчин. Ему переводить, а он лыка не вяжет.
issues.translation_quote: We had a German interpreter. When asked to translate, he spoke gibberish.
issues.justification: 'лыка не вяжет' means he was too drunk to speak coherently; 'gibberish' loses the drunkenness.

issues.source_quote: Мы его в кипятке и сварили.
issues.translation_quote: So we boiled him alive.
off the cuff

issues.source_quote: Нам надо посоветоваться с товарищами. Зайдите на недельке.
issues.translation_quote: We'll have to consult our comrades. Come back sometime next week.
Well, there you are!

issues.source_quote: Оставь меня, старушка, я в печали.
issues.translation_quote: Leave me, old woman, I am in sorrow.
Frankly, yes!

issues.source_quote: Вы гляньте на нашего активиста! Это же вооруженный бандит!
issues.translation_quote: Look at our community leader! He's an armed criminal!

issues.source_quote: Я не пьющий. С кинжалом. Хол
issues.translation_quote: No, I haven't been drinking. He has a dagger.

issues.source_quote: Зря снял! Не царская у тебя физиономия.
issues.translation_quote: You shouldn't have taken that off! You don't have a royal face.
Hello, I’m the Tsar, very pleased to meet you. The Tsar, very pleased. Tsar, very pleased. Hello, the Tsar.
issues.justification: Garbled and invented text: the source is Bunsha's flustered repeated greeting; the translation adds 'I'm the Tsar' and scrambles the stammering, and uses curly quotes inconsistent with the rest.

issues.source_quote: Вот Вы говорите, царь, царь. А Вы думаете, Марья Васильевна
issues.translation_quote: You keep saying, "Tsar, Tsar." But do you think, Maria Vasilyevna
issues.justification: Misnaming is a deliberate gag (Marfa/Maria/Margarita/Margo) and is preserved; fine.

issues.source_quote: Это нам не тили-тили, Это мы не трали-вали.
issues.translation_quote: No tee-lee-tee-lee for us, no tra-la-la for us.
issues.justification: The Russian idiom 'тили-тили, трали-вали' (idle nonsense/silly business, from 'тили-тили тесто') is rendered literally; sense is lost.

issues.translation_quote: That's a nickname! Quiet! Your surname?
A wolf's your boyar!
issues.justification: The idiom 'Тамбовский волк тебе товарищ' is lost; 'Tambov wolf' reference removed, flattening the joke.

issues.source_quote: Тоже мне, Тарапунька и Штепсель нашелся.
issues.translation_quote: Listen to this comedy duo!
issues.justification: Cultural reference to Soviet comedy duo is generalized; acceptable but loses flavor. Minor.

issues.source_quote: Казань брал, Астрахань брал, Ревель брал, Шпака не брал.
issues.translation_quote: I took Kazan, Astrakhan and Reval. I did not take Shpak.
I'll always have time to serve a sentence.
issues.justification: The pun on 'сесть' (to sit down to write / to be jailed) is partly kept but the dissertation line is acceptable.

issues.translation_quote: Why, you hooligan!
I feel faint!

issues.source_quote: Ну что ж, придется повысить напряжение. Опасно? Конечно, опасно! Но риск, как говорится...
issues.translation_quote: But nothing ventured...
issues.justification: Adaptation of 'риск — благородное дело' proverb; works acceptably.

issues.source_quote: Дело в том, что, минуя все эти стенки, я могу пронзить пространство.
issues.translation_quote: By bypassing these walls, I can pierce space.
- Where did the wall go? - What? What's this?
Vague doubts haunt me.
issues.justification: The recurring literary-parody quote (from Soviet comedy via Griboedov/Pushkin-esque register) is rendered plainly, and is varied between occurrences; the intended mock-theatrical register is lost.

issues.source_quote: Вы до которого часа сегодня работаете?
issues.translation_quote: What time do you finish work today?
Keep your mouth open!

issues.source_quote: Три раза я разводилась. Ну да, три. Зюзина я не считаю.
issues.translation_quote: I've been divorced three times. Yes, three. I'm not counting Zyuzin.

issues.source_quote: Прощай, Шурик. Только ты меня пока не выписывай.
issues.translation_quote: Just don't take my name off the apartment registration yet.

issues.source_quote: Они любят друг друга. Ну и пусть будут счастливы.
issues.translation_quote: They love each other. Let them be happy.

issues.source_quote: Я Вам как представитель общественности заявляю: прекратить!
issues.translation_quote: As a representative of the community, I demand that you stop!
Nonsense! I must have hit my head hard!

issues.source_quote: Это же вооруженный бандит! Смерд! - От смерда слышу!
issues.translation_quote: Cur! - Takes one to know one!
issues.justification: 'Смерд' (serf/lowborn) rendered as 'Cur', and the later 'serf' is then used, inconsistent for the same insult.

issues.translation_quote: serf
issues.justification: 'Холоп' (bondsman/slave-servant) rendered as 'serf', while 'смерд' is also 'serf'/'cur' variously; inconsistent terminology for distinct archaic terms.

issues.source_quote: Вы дo которого часа сегодня работаете? Говорит одна артистка.
issues.translation_quote: This is an actress.
Now, this was a good call!
Scenes are so exhausting.
Well, things are settling down.
Farewell, Prince! Good luck!
